lines.text: Liquid oxygen is attracted to a magnet, meaning it has unpaired electrons. But the standard Lewis structure shows all electrons paired. We need molecular orbital theory.

Two atomic orbitals always combine to form two molecular orbitals. Two one s orbitals combine in phase to form a lower-energy sigma bonding orbital, and out of phase to form a higher-energy sigma star antibonding orbital with a node. Bond order is bonding minus antibonding electrons, divided by two. H two has a bond order of one. He two plus has bond order one half. He two has bond order zero, so no stable bond is predicted.
In period two, s orbitals form sigma two s and sigma star two s. Head-on p overlap forms sigma two p, while side-by-side overlap forms two degenerate pi two p orbitals.

For oxygen and fluorine, a large energy gap between two s and two p orbitals means sigma two p lies below pi two p. But for boron, carbon, and nitrogen, the gap is small. The sigma two s and sigma two p orbitals interact, pushing sigma two p above pi two p.

Aufbau, Pauli, and Hund's rule apply to molecular orbitals. Filling oxygen, the last two electrons go singly into the degenerate pi star two p orbitals, explaining its paramagnetism. For boron, s p mixing places pi two p below sigma two p. Its highest two electrons singly occupy the pi two p orbitals, making boron paramagnetic too, which is evidence for s p mixing.

Let's compare the oxygen series by removing or adding pi star electrons. O two plus has bond order two point five and length one hundred twelve picometers. O two has bond order two and length one hundred twenty one. Adding electrons makes superoxide, O two minus, at about one hundred thirty four, and peroxide, O two two minus, at one hundred forty nine. Higher bond order means a stronger, shorter bond.
Watch out for these pitfalls. S p mixing is an interaction, not sp hybridisation. Sigma is not always below pi. And bond order zero means no stable bond predicted, not that molecules cannot exist.

Key takeaways. N atomic orbitals make N molecular orbitals. Bond order predicts stability. The two s two p gap dictates filling order. Molecular orbital theory explains paramagnetism. And standard rules fill molecular orbitals just like atomic orbitals.
